subject.title: [Feature]: Improve gateway stop/uninstall to handle system-level LaunchDaemons

question: What privileged macOS LaunchDaemon lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for gateway services?
rationale: The code change is not just a stop/uninstall implementation detail; it decides sudo/operator UX, root-owned plist mutation, execution user, service environment durability, and coexistence with user LaunchAgents.

options.title: Explicit system scope with safe default
options.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as the default, add an explicit audited system-scope lifecycle or guidance flow, and align install/status/stop/uninstall/doctor/docs/tests before implementation.

options.title: Diagnostic guidance only
options.body: Do not manage system LaunchDaemons from OpenClaw yet; improve status/doctor guidance so operators can safely use launchctl manually.

options.title: Full managed LaunchDaemon mode
options.body: Add first-class install/status/start/stop/uninstall support for LaunchDaemons, accepting the larger privileged-service surface after owner review.

recommendation.title: Explicit system scope with safe default
recommendation.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as the default, add an explicit audited system-scope lifecycle or guidance flow, and align install/status/stop/uninstall/doctor/docs/tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal ties steipete to the gateway lifecycle command introduction, service adapter registration, and prior maintainer review context for this issue.
